invocation: user-only: disable-model-invocation is true, so Claude Code blocks an automatic load and will not preload the skill into a sub-agent
_howto: This is not a trigger eval. The skill cannot be model-invoked, so 'would Claude load this on its own' is not a question with an answer any more. What is still worth testing is the two things a user-only skill can get wrong: acting on a request nobody invoked it for, and stretching to cover a request it was invoked on but does not fit. `invoked` says whether the user typed /story-refinery or named the skill; `expect` is the behaviour that is correct given that.

expectations.answer directly: Handle the request as an ordinary question. Do not run the phases, do not produce a bundle, and do not paraphrase the method as if it had been invoked.
expectations.refine: In scope. Run the phases in order and stop at the first gate the item genuinely fails, reporting that as the finding.
expectations.decline, not refinement: Invoked, but there is no backlog item here. Say so in a sentence and answer the underlying question if it has one.
expectations.stop and ask: Invoked and in scope, but the item does not carry enough to refine. Put the questions to the user with your best guess attached; do not decompose.
expectations.propose a split, refine one story: Invoked on an epic. Map it, propose the split, refine one story properly.
expectations.refuse to decompose: Invoked, but the item's own labels say refinement is the wrong instrument right now.
